'Is thessarine to' is asymmetric..why: Thessarine is a coined word: 0 hits in Dolma and none on Wikipedia, so it has no built-in direction. Giving a made-up relation a property contradicts nothing real.

sources.quote: In geometry, a square is a regular quadrilateral. It has four straight sides of equal length and four equal angles.

A triangle has five sides..why: Deliberately false side fact: a triangle has three sides.

sources.quote: A triangle or trigon is a polygon consisting of three sides connected at three corners.

notes: Dev RBox expansion, paired with mathematics-replace-d006 ('is parallel to' symmetric -> asymmetric): a made-up relation, thessarine_to (staging, fictional, no tags before the insert), is given the property the revision gives parallel_to, asymmetry, so revision and expansion send the model to the same conclusions and differ only in whether symmetry had to be pushed out (the ABox analogue keeps the new object). The instances use real lines (the x-axis, the y-axis, the line y = 2) as the paired revision uses lines. 'Thessarine' is a coined adjective with no built-in direction or mutuality. Yes and no are balanced as in the revision: direct (yes), the converse (no) and whether it is ruled out (yes); the cross-lingual prompts ask the first instance, keeping the coined word untranslated. After review the converse is asked as 'Could the y-axis also be thessarine to the x-axis?' (zh, es the same), not 'Does it follow that ...?': 'no' to the latter is also what any model says about a made-up relation it knows nothing about, so it passed without the edit, whereas 'could also' needs the asymmetry for 'no'. The coined word was changed from 'vellarine' (55 hits in Dolma) to 'thessarine' (0 hits, none on Wikipedia). Unrelated near asks the same property of a real line relation ('is perpendicular to', not asymmetric): an editor that spreads asymmetry to other line relations answers yes. It replaces the earlier functional has_quorvel_partner insert, which did not pair with the revision's property.
